learningObjective.title: Explain the processes of project procurement management

questions.question: A hospital's IT project needs a specialized scheduling system, and the team decides to acquire it from an external vendor rather than build it internally. In the slides' terms, what is the team doing?

options.A: Project procurement: buying goods or services from an outside source
options.B: Resource management: assigning the organization's own staff to tasks
options.C: Integration management: coordinating the work of all the knowledge areas
options.D: Scope management: defining exactly what the project will deliver

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** Procurement means acquiring goods and/or services from an outside source; project procurement management is acquiring them for a project from outside the performing organization. (LO1: Project Procurement Management)
**Why not B:** Resource management deals with internal resources, not acquiring from an outside source.
**Why not C:** Integration is a separate knowledge area; buying from an outside vendor is procurement.
**Why not D:** Scope management defines the work; obtaining it from a vendor is procurement.

questions.question: A project manager is tracking a vendor's contract performance, negotiating a change to the delivery schedule, and preparing to close out the contract. Which procurement process is this?

options.A: Identifying the procurement need
options.B: Planning procurement management
options.C: Conducting procurements
options.D: Controlling procurements

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** Controlling procurements means managing relationships with sellers, monitoring contract performance, making changes as needed and closing out contracts. (LO1: Project Procurement Management, Main Processes)
**Why not A:** Identifying the need is a pre-award activity; this work happens after award.
**Why not B:** Planning decides what to procure, and when and how; this contract is already in place.
**Why not C:** Conducting procurements obtains seller responses, selects sellers and awards contracts, which is already done here.

questions.question: After issuing bid documents, a project team collects vendor proposals, chooses the most suitable seller and awards the contract. Which procurement process does this describe?

options.A: Controlling procurements
options.B: Closing the project or phase
options.C: Planning procurement management
options.D: Conducting procurements

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** Conducting procurements is obtaining seller responses, selecting sellers and awarding contracts. (LO1: Project Procurement Management, Main Processes)
**Why not A:** Controlling manages seller relationships and contract performance after award.
**Why not B:** Closing comes at the end, in the post-award phase.
**Why not C:** Planning determines what to procure and when and how to do it, before any responses come in.

questions.question: A buyer from a commercial firm says their team is now in the 'manage contracts' and 'administer contracts' stage. Using the slides' PMBOK and commercial terminology comparison, where does this fall?

options.A: Award phase: Conduct Procurement
options.B: Post-award phase: Control Procurement and closing
options.C: Pre-award phase: Develop Competitive Solicitation
options.D: Pre-award phase: Plan Procurement Management

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** In the comparison, the post-award phase pairs PMBOK's Control Procurement and Close Project or Phase with the commercial terms Manage Contracts and Administer Contracts. (LO1: PMBOK Guide and Procurement Terminology Comparison)
**Why not A:** The award phase matches Conduct Competitive Solicitation and Conduct Negotiations.
**Why not C:** Developing the solicitation happens before award, not while contracts are being administered.
**Why not D:** Pre-award matches the commercial steps Identify Procurement Need and Develop Competitive Solicitation.

questions.question: A software firm's project manager is delivering a system to a client, and for the same project is buying servers from a hardware supplier. How do the slides describe the project manager's two roles?

options.A: Seller in both relationships, managing a contract with each party
options.B: Buyer from the client, managing procurement; seller to the supplier, managing a contract
options.C: Seller to the client, managing a contract; buyer from the supplier, managing procurement
options.D: Buyer in both relationships, managing procurement with each party

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** The slides show the project manager as seller to the customer (contract management) and as buyer from a supplier (procurement management). (LO1: Project Manager, Buyer vs. Seller)
**Why not A:** The project manager buys from the supplier, so that relationship is procurement management.
**Why not B:** This reverses the roles: the client buys from the project manager, who buys from the supplier.
**Why not D:** The project manager sells to the client, so that relationship is contract management.

questions.question: A municipality outsources its payroll system so its own staff can concentrate on delivering city services, while gaining access to the vendor's specialized technology. Which reasons for outsourcing does this reflect?

options.A: Focusing on the core business and accessing skills and technologies
options.B: Avoiding procurement planning by handing everything to one vendor
options.C: Guaranteeing lower costs no matter how the contract is managed
options.D: Removing the need for the city to oversee the vendor's work

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** The slides list accessing skills and technologies, reducing fixed and recurrent costs, focusing on the core business, flexibility and increased accountability as reasons to outsource. (LO1: Importance of Project Procurement Management)
**Why not B:** Outsourcing still requires planning, conducting and controlling procurements.
**Why not C:** Cost reduction is a goal, but the NYC cost overruns show it isn't guaranteed.
**Why not D:** The NYC examples show outsourced IT still needs strong oversight by the buyer.

questions.question: A city's outsourced payroll system ends up costing far more than planned, partly because of fraud and weak management of major IT projects. What lesson do the slides' New York City examples point to?

options.A: Outsourcing reliably reduces the total cost of IT projects
options.B: Outsourced IT still needs strong oversight by the buyer
options.C: Contractor fraud can't happen once a contract is signed
options.D: Large IT projects should never be outsourced at all

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** New York's mayor acknowledged City Hall had mismanaged major IT projects and vowed better oversight; CityTime's price was inflated by fraud and Nycaps' cost rose from $66 million to over $363 million. (LO1: Debates and Global Issues on Outsourcing)
**Why not A:** The NYC projects show outsourcing can go badly over budget.
**Why not C:** CityTime's price tag was inflated by fraud after contracting.
**Why not D:** The slides present a debate: some firms outsource little, others a lot.

questions.question: A US company moves its software-testing work from overseas back to a domestic urban centre that trains and employs low-income adults. Which recent approach do the slides call this?

options.A: Routine COTS buying
options.B: Interdivisional procurement
options.C: Urban onshoring
options.D: Strategic teaming

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Urban onshoring brings IT jobs back to the US, especially functions like software testing; the Urban Development Center model builds technology training and jobs in low-income urban neighbourhoods. (LO1: Debates and Global Issues on Outsourcing)
**Why not A:** COTS buys are routine purchases of standard items or services.
**Why not B:** That's buying work from another division of the same company.
**Why not D:** Teaming divides a major project among separate companies under a teaming agreement.

questions.question: A company runs its payroll every two weeks as ongoing operations, and separately launches a one-time effort to move payroll onto a new cloud system by March. Using the PMBOK definition in the slides, which of these is a project?

options.A: Both, since each involves planned work and a budget
options.B: The migration: a temporary effort with a unique result
options.C: The payroll runs, since they repeat on a set schedule
options.D: Neither, unless outside vendors are hired to do it

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** The slides quote PMBOK: a project is a temporary endeavour undertaken to create a unique product, service or result; the regular payroll runs are repetitive operations. (LO1: What Is a Project?)
**Why not A:** Planned, budgeted work isn't enough; a project is temporary and creates something unique.
**Why not C:** Work that repeats on a schedule is ongoing operations, not a temporary endeavour.
**Why not D:** Using vendors is a procurement choice; it doesn't decide whether work is a project.

questions.question: A project manager is sorting the project's 'buy' decisions using the slides' framework. Which list gives the three generic procurement categories?

options.A: Strategic teaming, interdivisional and all other routine procurements
options.B: Big, small and highly risky procurements of any kind
options.C: Major complexity, minor complexity and all other routine procurements
options.D: Design, performance and functional procurements

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Buying from outside sources splits into three generic categories (major complexity, minor complexity and routine procurements) and two special relationships (strategic teaming and interdivisional). (LO1: Make with Own Staff or Buy from Outside Sources)
**Why not A:** Strategic teaming and interdivisional work are the two special relationships, not generic categories.
**Why not B:** Those describe how procurements differ, not the three generic categories.
**Why not D:** Those are types of specifications, not procurement categories.

questions.question: A city has hired a firm to design a new commercial centre. Both parties have made major financial commitments, there's strong resistance to switching suppliers, and further competition is waived while quality stays high and pricing seems reasonable. Which category of procurement is this?

options.A: Minor complexity procurement
options.B: Major complexity procurement
options.C: Routine COTS procurement
options.D: Interdivisional procurement

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** Major complexity procurements involve major financial commitments by both parties, strong resistance to changing suppliers without compelling justification, and competition often waived while quality and pricing stay acceptable. (LO1: Major Complexity Procurements)
**Why not A:** Minor complexity buys are commercially available items bought with little or no modification.
**Why not C:** Routine buys are standard items or services handled with basic purchasing principles.
**Why not D:** Interdivisional work is bought from another division of the same company.

questions.question: A project includes developing a new airplane design through an outside firm. Based on the slides, how should the project handle this procurement?

options.A: Rebid it often so the supplier stays competitive
options.B: Treat it as a routine buy and identify it in a later phase
options.C: Substitute comparable items whenever they are cheaper
options.D: Identify it early and give it its own dedicated team

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** For major complexity procurements, early identification is critical to plan and organize them, and firms using an integrated project team approach often create a separate team for each; they're also prone to scope creep. (LO1: Major Complexity Procurements)
**Why not A:** Further competition is often waived on these buys while quality and pricing remain acceptable.
**Why not B:** Late identification suits routine COTS buys, not a major complexity procurement like a new airplane.
**Why not C:** Substitution of comparable items is a feature of minor complexity buys, not new development.

questions.question: A transit agency buys several existing buses from a manufacturer's standard product line, with only minimal modifications. The order is worth millions. Which category of procurement is this?

options.A: Major complexity procurement
options.B: Routine COTS procurement
options.C: Strategic teaming procurement
options.D: Minor complexity procurement

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** Minor complexity procurements often involve large monetary values, but the items exist, conform to the seller's existing specifications, are commercially available and are bought with little or no modification. (LO1: Minor Complexity Procurements)
**Why not A:** The buses already exist in the seller's line; nothing new is being created, despite the large dollar value.
**Why not B:** Routine buys are low-value standard items like fasteners or routine services, not high-value vehicles.
**Why not C:** Teaming involves companies dividing a major project under a teaming agreement.

questions.question: Midway through a plant expansion, a project manager realizes the large standard-model electrical generators still haven't been ordered, and their lead time threatens the schedule. What do the slides say should have happened?

options.A: They should have been bought under a teaming agreement
options.B: They needed early identification to plan lead time and funds
options.C: They should have had a separate integrated project team
options.D: They didn't need early identification, since they're standard items

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** For minor complexity buys, early identification is important in order to schedule the lead time for each item and budget the necessary funds. (LO1: Minor Complexity Procurements)
**Why not A:** Teaming agreements are for dividing major projects among companies, not buying standard generators.
**Why not C:** Separate teams are suggested for major complexity procurements.
**Why not D:** Late identification suits routine COTS buys; minor complexity buys need early identification for lead time.

questions.question: A project manager is deciding how much planning effort to give to buying fasteners, sheet metal and paint, plus an outsourced cafeteria service. What do the slides suggest?

options.A: Manage each one as a critical subproject with its own contract team
options.B: Use basic purchasing; identify them in later phases
options.C: Use teaming agreements so the risks are shared with suppliers
options.D: Identify them first, since they drive the project's critical schedule

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** Routine COTS buys rely on the fundamental principles of basic purchasing, and their early identification is typically not vital; they can be identified in later phases without causing difficulties. (LO1: Routine Buys of COTS Items or Purchased Services)
**Why not A:** Managing complicated contracts as subprojects fits major complexity buys, not routine ones.
**Why not C:** Teaming agreements are strategic, high-dollar accords between executives.
**Why not D:** The slides say early identification of routine buys is typically not vital.

questions.question: A long-time supplier of standard industrial pumps can't ship the usual model on time, and offers a different model with comparable performance that meets all of the project's requirements. What do the slides say about this kind of minor complexity buy?

options.A: A comparable item may be substituted if it meets the needs
options.B: A teaming agreement is needed before any change is made
options.C: It must be rebid as a major complexity procurement instead
options.D: Substitution is never allowed once a model is specified

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** Although minor complexity items are bought through long-term buyer–seller relationships, comparable-performance items may sometimes be substituted as long as they satisfy the same project requirements. (LO1: Minor Complexity Procurements)
**Why not B:** Teaming agreements are for strategic, high-dollar projects split between companies.
**Why not C:** The pumps are still commercially available items; a substitute doesn't make the buy major complexity.
**Why not D:** The slides allow comparable substitutes for minor complexity buys.

questions.question: A firm's outsourced development of a brand-new software package keeps growing as stakeholders add features partway through. According to the slides, what is this a typical sign of in a major complexity procurement?

options.A: Scope creep, which these procurements often experience
options.B: A shift of the buy into the minor complexity category
options.C: A problem that early identification prevents entirely
options.D: A reason to switch suppliers immediately and rebid

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** The slides note that major complexity procurements often experience a phenomenon called scope creep, which is one reason early identification and a dedicated team matter. (LO1: Major Complexity Procurements)
**Why not B:** Minor complexity buys are existing commercial items, not new development.
**Why not C:** Early identification helps plan and organize these buys; the slides don't say it removes scope creep.
**Why not D:** The slides note strong resistance to changing suppliers without compelling justification.

questions.question: The executives of two aerospace firms sign an overriding corporate agreement to split a new system into parts, each built by one company, combining their assets, facilities and people and sharing the risks. What kind of procurement is this?

options.A: A minor complexity buy of commercially available items
options.B: A major complexity buy from a single prime supplier
options.C: An interdivisional procurement within one company
options.D: A special procurement under a strategic teaming agreement

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** Teaming agreements (alliances or arrangements) are strategic, high-dollar accords between corporate executives that divide a major project into parts, each assigned to a separate company, combining assets and sharing risks. (LO1: Special Procurements, Strategic Teaming Agreements)
**Why not A:** The system is new and divided between companies, not bought off the shelf.
**Why not B:** Here two companies jointly divide the work under an overriding legal agreement.
**Why not C:** Interdivisional work is bought from another division of the same company, not a separate firm.

questions.question: Two companies forming a teaming arrangement for a new project ask how the work can be structured between them. What do the slides say?

options.A: Only as equal partners, with no company acting as prime
options.B: As prime contractor and subcontractor, or as associates
options.C: As a routine catalogue purchase from each partner
options.D: As an interdivisional transfer of work within one company

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** Teaming arrangements can create a prime contractor–subcontractor relationship, in which the designated prime receives the contract, or an 'associate' type of relationship. (LO1: Special Procurements, Strategic Teaming Agreements)
**Why not A:** The slides say a designated prime company may receive the contract.
**Why not C:** Teaming covers strategic, high-dollar work, not routine purchases.
**Why not D:** Teaming is between separate companies, not divisions of one firm.

questions.question: A project buys engineering work from another division of the same company. Costs keep accumulating, accountants move project dollars without regard to the value delivered, and neither division's executive wants to confront the other. What do the slides say about this kind of procurement?

options.A: It's reliably the easiest, since both divisions share goals
options.B: It's governed by a formal teaming agreement between firms
options.C: It should be easiest, but often proves the most painful
options.D: It must always be managed as a major complexity buy

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Interdivisional work should be the easiest arrangement but too often is the most painful: projects don't get respect, interdivisional costs are hard to shut off, and executives at the same level avoid confrontation. (LO1: Special Procurements, Interdivisional Work)
**Why not A:** The slides say it too often turns out to be the most painful arrangement.
**Why not B:** Teaming agreements are between separate companies, not divisions.
**Why not D:** Interdivisional work can fall into any of the three procurement categories.

questions.question: On a government-funded defence project, a manager plans to give a large work package to a sister division without any competition. What do the slides warn?

options.A: Government may insist on a formal competitive process
options.B: Interdivisional work is exempt from government procurement rules
options.C: Government prefers work to stay inside one company
options.D: Government always treats interdivisional work as 'make' work

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** Government wants the lowest price for work under its contracts and will often insist on formal solicitation, formal evaluation, source selection and a documented competitive procurement process, even for interdivisional work. (LO1: Special Procurements, Interdivisional Work)
**Why not B:** The slides describe government insisting on formal processes for such work.
**Why not C:** Government's priority is the lowest price, often through competition.
**Why not D:** Government may treat it as either make or buy work, depending on the point it's stressing.

questions.question: A manufacturer moves from many suppliers chosen on price to one supplier that shares forecasts, opens its books and joins product development early. Which relationship does the slides' spectrum say it now has?

options.A: A transactional relationship, with little trust
options.B: An interdivisional relationship, with shared profits
options.C: A routine COTS relationship, with basic purchasing
options.D: An alliance, marked by institutional trust

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** On the spectrum, alliances sit at the high-trust (institutional) end, with one or few suppliers, open books, shared forecasts and many early contributions to new products. (LO1: Spectrum of Supply Relationships and Institutional Trust)
**Why not A:** Transactional relationships use many suppliers, focus on price and share no forecasts.
**Why not B:** Interdivisional work is within one company, not with an outside supplier.
**Why not C:** Routine buying relies on basic purchasing principles, not deep integration.

questions.question: A buyer chooses suppliers mainly on price, relies on incoming inspection for quality, deals with many suppliers and expects that supply disruptions are possible. Where does this sit in the slides' characteristics of relationships?

options.A: Collaborative
options.B: Alliance
options.C: Transactional
options.D: Strategic teaming

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** In the characteristics table, transactional relationships focus on price, rely on incoming inspection, use many suppliers, have low trust and treat supply disruptions as possible. (LO1: Characteristics of Three Types of Relationships)
**Why not A:** Collaborative relationships sit between the two extremes, with more trust than described here.
**Why not B:** Alliances focus on total cost, design quality into the system, use one or few suppliers and make disruptions unlikely.
**Why not D:** Teaming is a special procurement relationship between companies sharing a major project.

questions.question: A buyer and a supplier rely mainly on good working relationships between the individuals who manage the account. They're well past a price-only, arm's-length approach, but haven't formed a full alliance. Where does this sit on the slides' spectrum of supply relationships?

options.A: Collaborative, resting on interpersonal trust
options.B: Interdivisional, resting on shared budgets
options.C: Transactional, resting on little trust
options.D: Alliance, resting on institutional trust

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** On the spectrum, transactional relationships carry little trust, collaborative relationships rest on interpersonal trust, and alliances rest on institutional trust. (LO1: Spectrum of Supply Relationships and Institutional Trust)
**Why not B:** Interdivisional work is done by another division of the same company.
**Why not C:** Transactional relationships are arm's-length and price-focused, which this one has moved past.
**Why not D:** An alliance is the far end of the spectrum, which these parties haven't reached.

questions.question: A project needs routine, off-the-shelf services from another division of the same company. According to the slides, does this interdivisional procurement need to be identified early?

options.A: Yes, since every interdivisional buy is high risk
options.B: Yes, since such work is always major complexity
options.C: Not usually, unless it creates something new
options.D: No, since interdivisional work needs no planning

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Early identification of many interdivisional procurements is typically not critical, unless the work involves creating something new as a Category 1 (major complexity) buy; interdivisional work can fall into any of the three categories. (LO1: Special Procurements, Interdivisional Work)
**Why not A:** The slides say early identification is typically not critical for many interdivisional buys.
**Why not B:** Interdivisional work can take any of the three procurement categories.
**Why not D:** It still needs managing; the slides only say early identification usually isn't critical.

questions.question: A project team concludes that every need can be met by the organization's own staff and equipment. According to the slides, what follows for procurement?

options.A: An RFI must be issued to confirm nothing should be bought
options.B: Every item must still go through make-or-buy analysis again
options.C: Conducting and controlling procurements must still be performed
options.D: No other procurement management processes need to be performed

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** If there's no need to buy any products or services from outside the organization, there's no need to perform any of the other procurement management processes. (LO1: Plan Procurement Management)
**Why not A:** The slides don't require an RFI; planning has already shown no outside buys are needed.
**Why not B:** The make-or-buy decision has been made: everything will be made internally.
**Why not C:** Those processes only apply when something is bought from outside.

questions.question: At the end of procurement planning, a project manager documents which components will be built internally and which will be bought. Which output of Plan Procurement Management is this?

options.A: The seller performance reviews
options.B: The closed-out contract files
options.C: The make-or-buy decisions
options.D: The awarded seller contracts

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Plan Procurement Management involves deciding whether, how, what, how much and when to procure; an important output is the make-or-buy decision. (LO1: Plan Procurement Management)
**Why not A:** Performance is monitored in Control Procurements.
**Why not B:** Close-out happens during Control Procurements.
**Why not D:** Contracts are awarded in Conduct Procurements, after planning.

questions.question: A new project manager asks what a procurement management plan actually covers. Which answer fits the slides?

options.A: A fixed template whose contents are identical on every project
options.B: The detailed technical specifications of each item to be bought
options.C: Only the final list of vendors chosen to supply the project
options.D: How procurement is managed, from purchase documents to closure

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** The procurement management plan describes how procurement will be managed, from developing documentation for outside purchases or acquisitions to contract closure; its contents vary with project needs. (LO1: Procurement Management Plan)
**Why not A:** The slides say the plan's contents vary based on project needs.
**Why not B:** Specifications belong to the SOW and requirement documents.
**Why not C:** The plan covers the whole procurement process, not just a vendor list.

questions.question: A project manager is gathering documents to start Plan Procurement Management. Which of these is listed in the slides as an input to the process?

options.A: The contracts signed with selected sellers
options.B: The risk register and stakeholder register
options.C: The close-out report for each contract
options.D: The proposals received from bidding sellers

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** Inputs include the project charter, business documents, the project management plan, project documents (requirements documentation, risk register, stakeholder register), EEFs and OPAs. (LO1: Plan Procurement Management, Inputs)
**Why not A:** Signed contracts come out of Conduct Procurements, later in the process.
**Why not C:** Close-out comes at the end, under Control Procurements.
**Why not D:** Proposals are received while conducting procurements.

questions.question: A project manager rushes requirements gathering, and later finds the procured equipment meets most of the project's needs, but not all of them. What do the slides say about this stage?

options.A: Defining the requirement details is the seller's responsibility
options.B: Meeting most of the needs is acceptable in procurement
options.C: Detailed requirements come first; this is where errors creep in
options.D: Requirements can be refined after the contracts are awarded

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** The first step in procurement planning is understanding the requirements for each work activity; errors arise from oversight or accepting resources that meet 'most' needs, so accurate, reliable information is essential. (LO1: Project Procurement Requirements)
**Why not A:** The project manager must gather and understand the requirements.
**Why not B:** The slides call meeting 'most' but not all needs a source of error.
**Why not D:** The slides put understanding requirements first, before procuring.

questions.question: A team building a custom lab for a client must decide which document to review first, and clarify in full with the client, before procurement. Which source do the slides call the primary source for the charter, checklists and WBS?

options.A: The bill of materials
options.B: The network diagram
options.C: The customer specifications
options.D: The regulatory requirements

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Customer specifications are the primary source used to develop the project charter, checklists and WBS; the team must review and clarify them with the customer, since most procurement information comes from them. (LO1: Procurement Information Sources)
**Why not A:** The BOM lists the specific items to be procured; it's built from the requirements, not the primary source.
**Why not B:** The network diagram sequences activities after the WBS is complete.
**Why not D:** Regulations add requirements beyond the customer's, but aren't the primary source.

questions.question: A project has no customer specification document. According to the slides, which document becomes the primary source of procurement information?

options.A: The project statement of work
options.B: The activity information checklist
options.C: The network diagram
options.D: The bill of materials

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** The project SOW, generated at the start of a project, outlines the deliverables and is used as the primary source of procurement information if the customer specification isn't available. (LO1: Procurement Information Sources)
**Why not B:** The checklist breaks deliverables into components, but it's built from the requirements and specifications.
**Why not C:** The network diagram sequences work activities.
**Why not D:** The BOM lists components to procure; it doesn't replace the customer specification as the primary source.

questions.question: A procurement analyst needs a list showing the quantity and exact part number or model of every component to be bought, sometimes naming the vendor an item must come from. Which document is this?

options.A: The statement of work
options.B: The work breakdown structure
options.C: The activity information checklist
options.D: The bill of materials (BOM)

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** A BOM is a specific list of items used to create a deliverable, listing quantities and actual part numbers or models of every component to be procured, and possibly required vendors. (LO1: Procurement Information Sources)
**Why not A:** The SOW describes the work required, not a parts list.
**Why not B:** The WBS breaks the deliverable into its smallest components and sequences them, without part numbers or vendors.
**Why not C:** The checklist organizes work activities, not parts and quantities.

questions.question: After the WBS and activity checklists are complete, a team maps which activities can run in parallel and which must finish before others start, so items are procured at the right time. Which source is this?

options.A: The project charter
options.B: The bill of materials
options.C: The customer specifications
options.D: The network diagram

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** The network diagram is developed after the WBS and activity information checklists to arrange work activities in sequence and analyze the flow of work, including parallel and dependent activities. (LO1: Procurement Information Sources)
**Why not A:** The charter may contain critical requirements, but it doesn't sequence activities.
**Why not B:** The BOM lists items and quantities, not activity sequence.
**Why not C:** Specifications detail what the customer needs, not the order of the work.

questions.question: A project manager overseeing a new food processing plant learns that the metal of storage containers and the hoses that move food must meet FDA stipulations. Which source of procurement information does this illustrate?

options.A: Regulatory requirements beyond the customer's
options.B: Design specifications written by the buyer
options.C: Customer specifications listed in the charter
options.D: Special requirements set by the customer

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** Regulatory requirements can go beyond customer requirements, covering items that state, local or federal regulations mandate; the FDA food plant is the slides' example. (LO1: Procurement Information Sources, Regulatory Requirements)
**Why not B:** The requirement comes from government regulation, not a buyer's design choices.
**Why not C:** The FDA rules apply regardless of what the customer specifies.
**Why not D:** These rules come from a regulator, not from the customer.

questions.question: A buyer writes a statement of work that describes only the work required under one particular contract. What do the slides call it, and what kind of document is it?

options.A: A bill of materials, which is a type of specification
options.B: A contract SOW, which is a type of scope statement
options.C: A procurement plan, which is a type of project charter
options.D: A requirements document, which is a type of RFP

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** A SOW describes the work required for the procurement; when used in a contract to describe only that contract's work, it's a contract SOW, a type of scope statement. A good SOW helps bidders understand the buyer's expectations. (LO1: Statement of Work)
**Why not A:** A BOM lists items and part numbers, not the work required.
**Why not C:** The procurement plan describes how procurement will be managed, not the work under one contract.
**Why not D:** An RFP is a bid document; the contract SOW is a scope statement.

questions.question: A hospital client insists that every new door in its wing come from a specific fire-rated product line the hospital has approved. Which procurement information source does this fall under, and what do the slides advise?

options.A: The bill of materials; let the supplier choose freely
options.B: The network diagram; sequence the door deliveries
options.C: Regulatory requirements; treat it as a legal mandate
options.D: Special customer requirements; interpret them with care

questions.note:
**Why D is correct:** Customers may have special requirements, and special care is needed in understanding them in order to correctly identify the special procurements they require. (LO1: Procurement Information Sources, Special Customer Requirements)
**Why not A:** A BOM may name required vendors, but this requirement comes from the customer and needs careful interpretation.
**Why not B:** The network diagram sequences activities; it doesn't capture the customer's product rule.
**Why not C:** This rule comes from the customer, not from state, local or federal regulations.

questions.question: A telecom project manager must decide whether the company's internal machine shop should produce a heat-sink housing with tight tolerances. Following the slides' example, what should the manager check before choosing to make it in-house?

options.A: Whether the shop can meet the specs, quality and schedule
options.B: Whether the shop manager would like to take on the work
options.C: Whether outside suppliers will lower their price
options.D: Only whether making the part in-house is cheaper

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** In the example, the project manager reviews the specifications with the machine shop manager, then evaluates the shop's quality level and when the item would be available before choosing the make option. (LO1: Procurement Decision Processes, Example)
**Why not B:** The test is capability, quality and timing, not preference.
**Why not C:** The make option depends on internal capability, not on supplier discounts.
**Why not D:** Cost matters, but the example stresses capability, quality and schedule.

questions.question: The machine shop manager says the heat-sink housing is beyond the shop's capability. According to the slides' example, what should the project manager do?

options.A: Source it externally, meeting the specs and schedule
options.B: Make it in-house anyway, since internal work is cheaper
options.C: Delay the project until the shop buys new equipment
options.D: Relax the tolerances so the shop can manage the part

questions.note:
**Why A is correct:** If the work is beyond internal capability, the project manager looks to external resources to make the item to all specified requirements and the delivery schedule, living with the cost of procuring it externally. (LO1: Procurement Decision Processes, Example)
**Why not B:** The example only uses internal resources when they're capable.
**Why not C:** The example's answer is to procure externally while keeping the schedule.
**Why not D:** The example requires meeting all of the specified requirements.

questions.question: A construction project manager must decide whether to purchase or rent a crane needed for a three-week activity. How do the slides frame decisions like this?

options.A: As contract closure decisions made after delivery
options.B: As source selection decisions made by a seller committee
options.C: As procurement decisions made in the project's best interest
options.D: As risk acceptance decisions made by the sponsor

questions.note:
**Why C is correct:** Procurement decisions include buying versus making, internal versus external resources, and purchasing versus renting equipment; they determine how things are obtained and the contract type, and should serve the project, budget, schedule and quality. (LO1: Procurement Decision Processes)
**Why not A:** Closure happens after the work; this decision is made in planning.
**Why not B:** Source selection chooses among sellers; this decision is how the crane is obtained.
**Why not D:** The slides treat purchase-or-rent as a procurement decision, not a risk response.

questions.question: A team new to buying lab robotics consults specialists inside and outside the organization, and studies the many potential suppliers before planning its purchases. Which planning tools and techniques is it using?

options.A: Bidder conferences and negotiations
options.B: Expert judgment and market research
options.C: Contract audits and close-out reviews
options.D: Change requests and lessons learned

questions.note:
**Why B is correct:** Plan Procurement Management tools include make-or-buy analysis, expert judgment from inside and outside experts, and market research, since many potential suppliers are often available. (LO1: Plan Procurement Management, Tools and Techniques)
**Why not A:** Those belong to conducting procurements, after planning.
**Why not C:** Those are part of controlling procurements.
**Why not D:** Those are outputs and updates, not planning tools.
